class.name: SkyClock
class.brief_description: Date, time and place on Earth: drives the sun and moon lights, the moon's phase and the stars' rotation.
class.description: Positions follow Meeus, [i]Astronomical Algorithms[/i] (2nd ed.): the sun from chapter 25 (about 0.01 deg), the moon from the main periodic terms of chapter 47 (about 0.001 deg against Meeus' worked example), apparent sidereal time from chapter 12 and the moon's phase and bright limb from chapter 48. The moon's parallax and atmospheric refraction (Saemundsson) are applied, so altitudes are what an observer sees. World axes: +Y up, -Z north (turned by [member north_offset]), +X east. Assign [member sun_light] and [member moon_light] and the clock points them; set [member time_scale] to run the clock. One update costs a few microseconds. See [code]docs/ideas/day-night.md[/code] in the repository and [code]docs/bench/sky --test[/code].

method.name: air_transmittance
method.description: Transmittance (red, green, blue) of Earth's clear air toward a body at [param altitude_degrees] above the horizon, seen from [param height] metres above sea level. It is the same table the sky's scattering atmosphere uses ([WeatherSkyMaterial]), so the lights and the sky agree. From sea level: about 0.94, 0.87, 0.76 at the zenith.

method.name: advance
method.description: Moves the clock forward by [param seconds] (backward if negative), rolling the date over.

method.name: get_celestial_basis
method.description: The rotation from the equatorial frame (x toward RA 0h, y toward RA 6h, z toward the north celestial pole) to world space, for placing stars by right ascension and declination.

method.name: get_ephemeris
method.description: The raw numbers in degrees, km and hours: [code]jd_ut, jd_tt, sun_lon, sun_ra, sun_dec, sun_distance_km, moon_lon, moon_lat, moon_ra, moon_dec, moon_distance_km, obliquity, lst_hours, sun_alt, sun_az, moon_alt, moon_az, moon_phase_angle[/code].

method.name: get_julian_day
method.description: The Julian day (UT) of the clock's date and time.

method.name: get_local_sidereal_time
method.description: Local apparent sidereal time in hours.

method.name: get_moon_altitude
method.description: The moon's apparent altitude in degrees (parallax and refraction applied).

method.name: get_moon_azimuth
method.description: The moon's azimuth in degrees from north through east.

method.name: get_moon_bright_limb_angle
method.description: Which way the lit side of the moon faces: the angle in degrees from the zenith direction on the sky, counterclockwise (toward the east limb). The moon's phase shading turns by this.

method.name: get_moon_direction
method.description: Unit vector from the scene toward the moon.

method.name: get_moon_distance
method.description: Earth-moon distance in km.

method.name: get_moon_illuminance_top
method.description: The moon's illuminance above the atmosphere in lux, from its magnitude (about 0.26 lux at full moon).

method.name: get_moon_illuminated_fraction
method.description: Fraction of the moon's disc that is lit, 0 (new) to 1 (full).

method.name: get_moon_magnitude
method.description: The moon's visual magnitude: -12.73 + 0.026 |a| + 4e-9 a^4 at phase angle a (Allen), corrected for distance.

method.name: get_moon_phase_angle
method.description: The sun-moon-Earth angle in degrees: 0 at full moon, 180 at new moon.

method.name: get_sun_altitude
method.description: The sun's apparent altitude in degrees (refraction applied when [member refraction] is on).

method.name: get_sun_azimuth
method.description: The sun's azimuth in degrees from north through east.

method.name: get_sun_direction
method.description: Unit vector from the scene toward the sun.

method.name: get_sun_distance
method.description: Earth-sun distance in km.

method.name: get_sun_illuminance_top
method.description: Sunlight above the atmosphere in lux (133,800 lux at 1 AU, Darula et al. 2005).

method.name: julian_day
method.description: Julian day of a Gregorian date; [param day] may carry a fraction (Meeus chapter 7).

method.name: set_julian_day
method.description: Sets the clock to a Julian day (UT); the local date and time follow [member utc_offset].

members.member: The clock sets each light's colour and [member Light3D.light_energy] from its body's brightness above the air ([method get_sun_illuminance_top], [method get_moon_illuminance_top]) times [method air_transmittance] at its altitude, scaled by [member energy_per_lux]. It also gives both bodies to the [WeatherSkyMaterial] of the scene's environment, whose scattering atmosphere then lights the sky, twilight and the Earth's shadow from them. Off, the lights keep the colour and energy set by hand.

[member Light3D.light_energy] for one lux. The default puts the noon sun near 1.1 and the full moon near 2.5e-6, a real ratio of about 450,000 to 1: night needs the exposure to follow (see [code]docs/ideas/exposure.md[/code]).
Hide each light while its body is below the horizon.
Observer latitude in degrees, north positive.
Observer longitude in degrees, east positive.
A [DirectionalLight3D] the clock points from the moon.
How far north is turned from world -Z toward +X, in degrees.
Lift bodies near the horizon by atmospheric refraction (about 0.57 deg at the horizon), as seen.
A [DirectionalLight3D] the clock points from the sun.
Simulated seconds per real second while the game runs; 0 stops the clock, 3600 is an hour a second.
The local clock's offset from UTC in hours (1 for Lisbon summer time).
